context.question: Should intrinsic revision motivate a frozen-model exact-answer reasoning project?
context.decision: Require a matched-budget reproduction before investing in an intrinsic revision mechanism
context.target_setting: Tool-free frozen LLM; target model/version/tasks unspecified
context.bounds: Three named historical papers; selected sections only; no current-field completeness, forward-citation audit or formal novelty search

papers.title: Self-Refine: Iterative Refinement with Self-Feedback
papers.main_claim: Same-model feedback/refinement improves a heterogeneous task mix; inspect math separately.

papers.title: Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet
papers.main_claim: Intrinsic reasoning correction struggles; oracle access, response budgets and prompts change claimed gains.

papers.title: CRITIC: Large Language Models Can Self-Correct with Tool-Interactive Critiquing
papers.main_claim: Tool-interactive verification/revision improves tested outputs; intrinsic ablations vary.

claims.statement: Self-Refine presents same-model iterative feedback/refinement and reports gains across a heterogeneous task mix.
claims.scope: Authors’ main method/evaluation claim; task metrics are heterogeneous.

evidence.observation: Same model drafts, critiques and revises; reported gains vary substantially by task, including small math changes recorded in C1.
evidence.analyst_inference: Read task-specific results before transferring the headline.

assessment.reason: Primary method and decisive results rechecked; scoped extraction only
assessment.limitation: A mixture of preference and task metrics is not a common reasoning effect size.

uses.decision: Recover the proposed loop and its main evaluation boundary
uses.transfer_assumption: Historical protocols do not establish effects for an unspecified target model or a different cost metric

claims.statement: Math results show small point-estimate changes, despite larger gains on other task metrics.
claims.scope: Table 1 model/task setups; not an equal-all-in-budget guarantee.

evidence.locator: Table 1, PDF p.5; §3.2–3.3; Appendix K.1, Table 14
evidence.observation: Math solve rates: 64.1→64.1, 74.8→75.0, 92.9→93.1. Authors also distinguish oracle feedback.
evidence.authors_interpretation: Difficulty recognizing errors limits math refinement.
evidence.analyst_inference: A general iterative-improvement headline is insufficient motivation for intrinsic exact-answer reasoning.

assessment.reason: Inspected primary PDF sections; strength applies only to reported scoped result
assessment.limitation: Point estimates are not evidence of zero effect; paired precision and equal-budget comparison not established here.

uses.transfer_assumption: New target models/tasks require direct testing

claims.statement: A more informative initial prompt changes the constrained-generation comparison.
claims.scope: CommonGen-Hard concept coverage; gpt-3.5-turbo-0613 replication; not a mathematical reasoning equivalence.

evidence.observation: Authors’ stronger initial prompt: 81.8; subsequent correction: 75.1 concept coverage.
evidence.authors_interpretation: Initial instruction quality can confound attributed correction gains.
evidence.analyst_inference: Test informative initial prompts before attributing gains to a revision mechanism.

assessment.reason: Inspected primary PDF sections; strength applies only to reported scoped result
assessment.limitation: This is a specific prompt intervention, not a theorem that intrinsic revision never works; all-in budgets differ.

uses.decision: Add stronger initial-prompt and cost controls
uses.transfer_assumption: Need analogous prompt adequacy in the target task

claims.statement: Tool-assisted and no-tool program revision have model/task-dependent reported effects.
claims.scope: Table 2 math-program synthesis; official test splits; up to four corrections; final program execution is distinct from revision feedback.

evidence.observation: GSM8K PoT→CRITIC: 72.5→78.2 (gpt-3.5) and 70.1→72.2 (text-davinci-003). No-tool deltas on GSM8K/SVAMP/TabMWP: +4.5/0/+12 and -1.8/-3.3/+20.3 pp, respectively.
evidence.authors_interpretation: External feedback is useful; intrinsic critique is less reliable.
evidence.analyst_inference: Retain positive and negative ablation rows and separate feedback access.

assessment.reason: Primary method and decisive results rechecked; scoped extraction only
assessment.limitation: Rows give point estimates without paired intervals; no all-in-token-matched pure-text comparison; denominator counts were not independently audited here. Internal reporting discrepancy: Table 2 gives Text-Davinci-003 GSM8K CRITIC 72.2, while Appendix D.6/Table 10 gives 71.2; this extraction uses Table 2 and does not resolve the discrepancy.

uses.decision: Avoid selecting favorable no-tool rows as the paper’s general conclusion
uses.transfer_assumption: Historical protocols do not establish effects for an unspecified target model or a different cost metric

claims.statement: Two intrinsic correction rounds reduce reported GSM8K accuracy in these model columns.
claims.scope: GPT-3.5-Turbo-0613 full GSM8K (1,319 items); GPT-4 sampled 200 items; temperature 1, no oracle stop; one to five calls.

evidence.authors_interpretation: Intrinsic reasoning correction is unreliable in the tested protocols.
evidence.analyst_inference: Treat unconditional intrinsic gain as an assumption to test, not an established motivation.

assessment.reason: Primary method and decisive results rechecked; scoped extraction only

claims.statement: Oracle stopping uses correctness labels and cannot establish intrinsic correction ability.
claims.scope: Ground-truth answer correctness controls continuation; distinct information regime from intrinsic stopping.

evidence.locator: §3.2; Table 2 contrasted with Table 3, PDF p.4
evidence.observation: Oracle GSM8K scores include 84.3% (GPT-3.5) and 97.5% (GPT-4); labels stop revision of correct answers.
evidence.authors_interpretation: Oracle gains do not demonstrate intrinsic self-correction.
evidence.analyst_inference: Keep answer-label access and stopping rules explicit.

assessment.reason: Primary method and decisive results rechecked; scoped extraction only
assessment.limitation: These tables do not estimate a universally transferable causal feedback effect.

uses.decision: Exclude oracle stopping from the tool-free method claim

claims.statement: At equal response counts, reported multi-agent debate accuracy is below self-consistency in this experiment.
claims.scope: GSM8K full test set, gpt-3.5-turbo-0301; three agents and two debate rounds; response count matched, not all-in tokens.

evidence.observation: Six responses: debate 83.2 vs self-consistency 85.3%; nine: 83.0 vs 88.2%.
evidence.authors_interpretation: Selection/self-consistency can explain gains attributed to debate.
evidence.analyst_inference: Include a strong resampling/selection control in a new experiment.

assessment.reason: Primary method and decisive results rechecked; scoped extraction only
assessment.limitation: Multi-agent debate is a different method from a single-model revision loop; token/call costs are not interchangeable.

uses.decision: Specify what a fair compute baseline must control
uses.transfer_assumption: Historical protocols do not establish effects for an unspecified target model or a different cost metric

claims.statement: CRITIC’s main method verifies initial output through tools and then revises a frozen model’s output.
claims.scope: Tool-interactive protocol; no training, not a purely intrinsic feedback mechanism.

evidence.observation: The verification/correction loop uses external evidence; C3 records the math comparison.
evidence.authors_interpretation: Tools help validate and correct output.
evidence.analyst_inference: Tool-based method evidence belongs to its own information regime.

assessment.reason: Primary method and decisive results rechecked; scoped extraction only
assessment.limitation: Does not prove tools are necessary for every possible intrinsic revision method.
